subject: Runtime economics & routing anchoring - private GPU grid sizing request
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@stratus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: committed throughput + network anchors for private GPU grid

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for taking this — were starting the procurement cycle at StratusAI and need a concrete sizing + routing proposal for a VPC/on-prem private GPU deployment. High level ask: give us a recommended baseline pool, a committed throughput target we can put in the contract (99th / sustained windows), and a short routing/egress checklist so our infra team can validate network boundaries.

Workload profile (attached):
- Model: Llama-2-70B / quantized variant (mostly int8 inference)
- Traffic: baseline sustained 60 qps, expected weekly spikes to 240 qps for 30-45 minute windows, occasional one-off bursts to ~500 qps for <5 minutes
- Request shape: median tokens 256, 95th tokens 1024; typical prompt prefilling (cache hit 30% for repeated prefixes)
- Latency target: P95 <= 300 ms wall-clock for streamed responses (well accept higher tail if we get throughput guarantees)
- Region: single US site (AWS Direct Connect to our VPC)
- Networking constraints: our egress budget is limited to 8 Gbps sustained, peaky bursts allowed but we'd like guidance on what to expect.

Can you give us a first-pass "committed throughput" number and recommended pool size (nodes / GPU types) plus the minimal routing/egress controls we should put on the contract? If you need any other inputs I can pull them from the attached workload csv.

Attachments: stratus_workload_profile.csv, existing_network_topology.drawio

Thanks,
Anya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@stratus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: committed throughput + network anchors for private GPU grid

Anya — thanks for the clear profile and attachments. Quick first-pass below; Marissa and Jonas are looped for cost/procurement and networking sanity-checks. I attached our runway calc and a short routing playbook with recommended egress policing and fallback lanes.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model perf: Llama-2-70B int8 ≈ 10–14 inference requests per second per A100-class GPU at avg 256 tokens (conservative: we use 12 req/s per GPU baseline).
- Cache warmup: 30% prefix hit reduces average token work by ~20% across the pool; we account for warm cache in the above perf estimate.
- Concurrency: requests are single-turn generative but frequently streamed. We budget for concurrent KV-cache costs separately (minor for this model).
- Target latency SLO: P95 <= 300ms — we'll design so that P95 is met at committed throughput; P99 will be higher under heavy bursts unless you buy burst capacity.

Sizing (recommendation):
- Committed baseline: 60 qps sustained -> pool compute needed = 60 qps / 12 req/s per GPU ≈ 5 GPUs.
- Operational margin (runway): we recommend 2.5x headroom for allowed sustained spikes and node failover -> baseline reserved = 5 * 2.5 = 12.5 -> round up to 13 GPUs reserved.
- Burst buffer (non-committed, on-demand): handle up to 500 qps short bursts by enabling a transient burst group sized at ~40 GPUs for <10 minutes. This can be contracted as an overage pool or via cloud burst.
- Networking: with your 8 Gbps egress constraint, streaming at P95 <=300ms and typical token sizes, we estimate ~2.6 Gbps sustained at 60 qps (accounting for streaming overhead). Peak bursts to 500 qps approach ~22 Gbps if fully streaming — that exceeds your stated egress. Recommendation: enable degraded-mode responses (batching + truncated streaming) for burst windows or contract additional burst egress.

Operational notes / contract language suggestions:
- Commit: reserved 13 GPUs for the private pool, with a parity clause for hardware replacement and a scheduled warmup window after major deploys (24–48h).
- Burst: define a burst SLU (short-lived units) priced separately; include throttling thresholds and a negotiated emergency uplift path.
- Observability: include token-level telemetry exports and P95/P99 traces for the committed model version.

Next steps: Marissa, can you produce a high-level pricing delta for reserved 13 GPUs + 40 GPU burst buffer? Jonas, please sanity-check the network math and routing_playbook.md for Direct Connect specifics (NAT, MTU, and egress shaping).

Attachments: runway_calc_v1.xlsx, routing_playbook.md

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@stratus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: committed throughput + network anchors for private GPU grid

Karthik / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear assumptions. We reviewed the runway calc and the numbers look sane. A few clarifying items before we hand this to procurement: 

1) Fallback behavior when egress is saturated
On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 11:30 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Recommendation: enable degraded-mode responses (batching + truncated streaming) for burst windows or contract additional burst egress.

Can you expand on the degraded mode? Specifically: will degraded-mode preserve completion correctness (but delay/compact streaming), or will it be lossy (e.g., drop intermediate tokens)? We need wording we can include in runbooks and an SLA appendix.

2) Warmup and cache priming window
We like the 24–48h warmup recommendation. Can you add a short procedure we can operationalize (simple steps our infra team runs before a marketing campaign): endpoints to ping, expected cache hit curves, and a checklist for validating warm cache after deploy?

3) Procurement ask
Procurement wants a firm committed throughput number and the exact hardware SKU mix. They also want to understand minimum lead times for hardware replacement and a contract addendum for temporary overage uplift. Can Marissa echo the pricing delta and a suggested clause for emergency uplift?

If you can send an updated runway calc that includes a short degraded-mode description and a 48h warmup checklist, we can start a PO draft next week.

Thanks — looping procurement so they can start internal approvals.

Best,
Anya
